properties.name: Pennsylvania Railroad Exchange Place terminal, train shed and approach tracks, Jersey City
properties.basis: Twelve-track, six-platform ferry terminal on wooden piers built by the PRR in 1873 (timeline); burnt 4 Aug 1884, rebuilt 1888-92 and raised 15-20 ft in 1891; the last PRR passenger train used it on 17 Nov 1961 and the last buildings were demolished in 1963 (Wikipedia 'Exchange Place (PRR station)': station point 40.71648 N 74.03238 W).
properties.outline: Hand-drawn polygon about the station point (east of Hudson Street, between Montgomery St and Exchange Place's present foot); no plan of the track layout was opened. +-60 m.

properties.name: Pennsylvania Railroad Harsimus Cove freight yards, stockyards, abattoir and car floats, Jersey City
properties.basis: PRR freight terminal at Harsimus Cove opened 1868 (timeline); cove filled by 1870 'for railyards' and 'extending a quarter mile from Henderson Street' (Marin Boulevard); 'huge stockyards dominated the waterfront between the train terminals', PRR abattoir to the south (Wikipedia 'Harsimus'); served by the Harsimus Stem Embankment. End year ESTIMATED: ports 'abandoned by the 1970s', Newport redevelopment began 1986.
properties.outline: Hand-drawn polygon: west edge Marin Boulevard / Henderson St line (-74.0405), north edge 6th Street's east end (lat 40.7250, from Overture's street lines), south edge about Christopher Columbus Drive, east edge the 1919-era shore. +-80 m.

properties.name: Harsimus Stem Embankment (PRR, seven tracks), Jersey City
properties.basis: Embankment built 1901-1905 (National Register nomination, via search snippet; the Wikipedia page gives no year); 27 ft high, seven tracks, south side of Sixth Street from Marin Boulevard west to Brunswick Street (Wikipedia 'Harsimus Stem Embankment'). Disused but still standing: end 9999.
properties.outline: Strip 35 m wide along the south side of 6th Street, using Overture's 6th Street centreline (-74.0404 40.7251 to -74.0488 40.7258). +-15 m. Track lines should be generated: no rail line is in today's data for it.

properties.name: Erie Railroad Pavonia Terminal and yards, Jersey City
properties.basis: Pavonia terminal opened 1 May 1861 (Wikipedia infobox; Erie began developing the site in 1856); new terminal 4 Dec 1887; closed 12 Dec 1958, demolished 1961. Built on the northern part of the filled Harsimus Cove; the Long Slip separated it from Hoboken Terminal. End year ESTIMATED as 1959 (cars gone after the passenger closing; demolition 1961).
properties.outline: Hand-drawn polygon about the terminal point (40.726676 N 74.034757 W): south edge the PRR yard's north edge, north edge the Long Slip, west edge the viaduct at the foot of the Palisades cut. +-80 m.

properties.name: Central Railroad of New Jersey Communipaw terminal and yards, Jersey City
properties.basis: Terminal of 1864 replaced 1889 (headhouse still stands); Bush trainsheds 1914; passenger service ended 30 April 1967; yards on filled land, 63 acres on the National Register (Wikipedia 'Central Railroad of New Jersey Terminal', point 40 42 26 N 74 02 07 W). End year is the passenger closing; freight use after 1967 not checked.
properties.outline: Hand-drawn polygon on today's Liberty State Park north end: the headhouse point, the surviving track block (-74.039..-74.036, 40.7068-40.7080) and the park's flat made ground west of it to the old Johnston Avenue line. +-100 m.

properties.name: Lehigh Valley Railroad Black Tom terminal and National Docks yards, Jersey City
properties.basis: National Docks Railway of 1883 connected the National Storage Company docks at Black Tom with the PRR (timeline); the Lehigh Valley ran the Black Tom terminal (blown up 30 July 1916: 'over one hundred railroad cars and warehouses', Wikipedia 'Black Tom explosion', point 40 41 32 N 74 03 20 W). End year ESTIMATED (Liberty State Park, opened 1976); the LV's 1889 South Cove freight terminal is not outlined.
properties.outline: Hand-drawn polygon about the Black Tom point on today's filled peninsula of Liberty State Park (Caven Point road area). No plan opened. +-150 m.

properties.name: Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Hoboken terminal and yard
properties.basis: First terminal 14 Nov 1862 (Morris & Essex), second 15 Jan 1868, burnt June 1873, fourth 1885, burnt 1905, present terminal 1907 (Wikipedia 'Hoboken Terminal', point 40.735 N 74.0275 W). The yard is still in use (NJ Transit): today's tracks are in rail.parquet already; this outline only widens the area to the old yard.
properties.outline: Hand-drawn polygon over today's yard throat (rail.parquet track fan) to the foot of the Bergen Hill cut. +-50 m.

properties.name: West Shore (New York Central) Weehawken terminal and yards
properties.basis: Terminal opened 1884, closed 1959 (last ferry 25 March 1959); sixteen passenger tracks, five ferry slips, car-float facilities and 'extensive yards' (Wikipedia 'Weehawken Terminal', point 40.771639 N 74.01275 W).
properties.outline: Hand-drawn strip 100-250 m wide between the West Shore line's surviving curve (today's Hudson-Bergen Light Rail, from the Weehawken Tunnel mouth) and today's shore, 40.763-40.775 N. The yard's length is not in the sources opened. +-100 m.

properties.name: Pennsylvania Railroad Greenville Yard and car-float bridges, Jersey City
properties.basis: Developed 1904 by the PRR with three car-float bridges (Nos. 11-13), No. 14 in 1910, No. 10 in 1924; fire 1 Jan 1931 destroyed the wooden bridges; yard still in use (Wikipedia 'Greenville Yard').
properties.outline: Hand-drawn polygon around today's yard track fan in rail.parquet (-74.093..-74.074, 40.676-40.688) read off a base map. +-60 m. Today's tracks cover most of it.
